identity.name: Kharijite imamate of Ifriqiya
alt_names: Ibadi imamate of Tripolitania and Ifriqiya

land.text: Tripolitania, where the Ibadites rose under their imam al-Harith

predecessors.note: The page dates neither the rising (after 747) nor its start in 751; 751 is Cliopatria's. In 757 the whole Fihrid territory follows.

land.text: Ifriqiya and Tripolitania, retaken by 'an Abbasid army' in 761

successors.note: The Kharijites page: 'Driven out by an Abbasid army in 761'; Cliopatria keeps the Kharijites to 762.

land.text: Tahart (Tahert), where the Ibadi leaders driven out in 761 'founded a state... later known as the Rustamid dynasty'

capitals.name: Kairouan (al-Qayrawan)
capitals.note: The Ibadites 'took Kairouan and established a Kharijite imamate over Ifriqiya' in 758; no page opened calls it the capital. Before that the imamate had no recorded seat (Tripoli was retaken in 757).

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid only in 751: Tripolitania held by the Ibadites under al-Harith until the Ifriqiyan army 'reconquered Tripolitana' in 752

keyframe_review.note: 105,812 km2 (Libya plus southern Tunisia). The page has the reconquest in 752, not 754; the 'remnants' fled into the Jebel Nafusa (see the 752 keyframe). The Ibadite takeover is undated on the page (imam al-Harith 'revolted' after Ilyas moved against the Ibadites in 747).

correction.text: the Ibadite remnants 'driven... into the Jebel Nafusa' after 752

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Kharijite shape for 755-756 and keeps the 751 shape to 754. After 752 the page leaves only remnants in the Jebel Nafusa until the Ibadites under Abu al-Khattab al-Ma'afiri retake Tripoli in 757. Reviewer (af-02-b, 2026-10-19): starts 752, the year of the Fihrid reconquest (/ledger/1), so that the Fihrid 752 keyframe and this one do not both hold Tripolitania in 752.

correction.text: unchanged shape for 757-761: Tripoli (757), Kairouan (Warfajuma and Sufris 757, Ibadites 758), Ifriqiya; ends 761

keyframe_review.note: 251,017 km2, the old Fihrid outline including about 64,000 km2 of eastern Algeria, which the Abd al-Rahman page says was out of Fihrid reach and no page opened gives to the imamate (unverified). The Kharijites page: 'In 757, Ibadis seized Tripoli and captured Kairouan the next year'; 'Driven out by an Abbasid army in 761'. Cliopatria's 762 is one year later than the page.

region.text: Tripolitania and southern Tunisia, held by the Ibadites under their imam al-Harith

ledger.note: 751: the Ibadites hold Tripolitania. The Abd al-Rahman page says the Ibadites 'revolted under the leadership of their imam al-Harith' after 747 and were beaten in 752, but gives no year for the rising; 751 is Cliopatria's first year.

region.text: Tripolitania, with the remnants driven into the Jebel Nafusa

ledger.note: 752: the Fihrids reconquer Tripolitania. 'In 752, Ibn Habib dispatched an Ifriqiyan army and reconquered Tripolitana from the Ibadites.'

region.text: Tripoli, retaken by the Ibadites under Abu al-Khattab al-Ma'afiri

ledger.note: 757: the Ibadites seize Tripoli. 'In 757, Ibadis seized Tripoli and captured Kairouan the next year.' The page names the city; the region is my reading.
757: Kairouan falls. 'Warfajuma Berbers and Sufrite allies captured Kairouan, killing Habib and ending the Fihrid dynasty.' Sufri Kharijites are the same state in Cliopatria's row.

758: the Ibadites take Kairouan from the Sufris and found the imamate. 'Ibadites took Kairouan and established a Kharijite imamate over Ifriqiya'; the Kharijites page puts the capture 'the next year' after 757. The state keeps its colour.

region.text: Ifriqiya and Tripolitania, reconquered by 'an Abbasid army'

ledger.note: 761: the Abbasids retake Ifriqiya. 'Driven out by an Abbasid army in 761', the Ibadi leaders founded a state in Tahart. The page names neither the commander nor the cities; the land is my reading from the earlier Kairouan and Tripoli events.

region.text: the imamate's last land in Ifriqiya

ledger.note: 761: the Kharijite imamate of Ifriqiya ends; the Ibadi leaders withdraw to Tahart (later the Rustamid dynasty). Cliopatria's last year is 762.

wars.name: Ibadite revolt in Tripolitania

zones.text: Tripolitania, with the Jebel Nafusa as refuge

wars.outcome: The Ibadites rise under imam al-Harith; the Fihrids reconquer Tripolitania in 752 and drive the remnants into the Jebel Nafusa.
wars.note: Same war as the Fihrid dossier's; the page does not date the rising.

wars.name: Kharijite conquest of Ifriqiya
wars.outcome: The Warfajuma and Sufris take Kairouan and kill Habib (757); the Ibadites retake Tripoli (757) and Kairouan (758).
wars.note: The Abd al-Rahman page puts the Sufri capture of Kairouan in 757 and the Ibadite one in 758.

wars.name: Abbasid reconquest of Ifriqiya
wars.outcome: An Abbasid army drives the Ibadite leaders out of Ifriqiya in 761; they found Tahart.
wars.note: The only dated sentence; the Abbasid commander is not named on the page (the Abd al-Rahman page does not cover 761).

certainty.note: Neither page names a frontier; the Algerian part of the 757 shape is unverified and the Saharan edge is approximate.

sources.title: Kharijites
sources.note: The sect page: Ibadis seize Tripoli 757 and Kairouan 758, Abbasid expulsion 761, Tahart; thin on the state itself.

sources.title: Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib al-Fihri
sources.note: The Ibadite revolt and 752 reconquest, the Jebel Nafusa remnants, Warfajuma at Kairouan 757, Tripoli 757, Ibadite imamate 758.

sources.title: Fihrids
sources.note: The 757-758 Kharijite uprising that ended the Fihrids.

notes: The Kharijites row is the Ibadi/Sufri regimes of Tripolitania and Ifriqiya, not the sect: the Cliopatria Name is the sect's, the page 'Kharijites' is the sect article (thin on this state). Cliopatria has no Kharijite shape for 755-756 and gives the 751 shape to 754 although the Fihrid reconquest of Tripolitania is 752; the Jebel Nafusa remnants stand in for 753-756. Which Kharijites held Kairouan in 757 (Warfajuma Sufris) and 758 (Ibadites under Abu al-Khattab al-Ma'afiri) is a faction change inside one row; a Sufri/Ibadi split into two dossiers could be argued but the pages are too thin. The Midrarids of Sijilmasa (Sufri, 'around 750', Kharijites page) are a separate state with no Cliopatria row (a dossier is needed). The Abbasid reconquest of 761 is the Kharijites page only; the Abbasid commander and the 762 year Cliopatria uses are not given. Tahart is the seat of the Rustamid dynasty (rustamid-dynasty dossier). Page budget 2: Kharijites and Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib al-Fihri; the Fihrids page (opened for the Fihrids dossier) is cited only for the 757-758 uprising.
